title: Unify quota reset semantics: rolling windows, calendar resets, and reserved-capacity accounting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Production customers are seeing mismatches between UI quota meters, billed usage, and token-level counters when tenants use a mix of hosted + reserved capacity. Root causes: (1) multiple reset strategies exist across components (calendar midnight reset, naive daily bucket, and ad-hoc rolling window implemented in two services); (2) reserved capacity is treated as a separate counter but decrement/restore logic races with the global usage ledger; (3) our rolling-window support uses coarse 24h buckets which mis-attribute tokens near boundaries. Goal: design and implement a single source-of-truth quota engine that supports both calendar (daily/monthly) resets and arbitrary rolling-window windows, plus a correct ledger for reserved capacity reservations and releases.
acceptance_criteria: All quota displays in Console and API agree with the billing ledger within 0 token drift for new requests after rollout
Rolling 24h and 30d windows computed per-tenant with bounded error & deterministic bucket boundaries
Reserved capacity reservations are atomic and cannot double-count against on-demand pools under burst scenarios
Backfill job can reconcile historical mismatches for the past 90 days and generate a reconciliation report
Integration tests cover time-travel scenarios (DST, month boundary, leap day) and tenant timezone edge cases
design_notes: Proposed approach: (A) Replace ad-hoc counters with time-windowed append-only event log (lightweight ledger) per tenant keyed by token_type and attribution (on-demand vs reserved). (B) Implement sliding-window aggregator that keeps N fixed buckets at 1h resolution for 30d window plus a special midnight calendar alignment pass for monthly quotas. (C) Introduce a reservation token lifecycle: reserve -> allocate (consume) -> release; reservations get a TTL and are reconciled by a background sweeper. (D) Expose a read path for Console and API that queries aggregated materialized views for speed; write path appends to ledger and updates in-memory rolling aggregates via a streaming changefeed. Trade-offs: increased write amplification and storage for the append-only ledger vs deterministic correctness and easier backfill. We'll cap retention for per-token events at 120 days and compress older buckets into summary rows.
implementation_steps: Add append-only per-tenant ledger table (series) with event_type, qty, token_type, source, timestamp
Implement sliding-window aggregator library in billing-service (Go) with deterministic bucket alignment and noop for sub-minute windows
Build atomic reservation API: /reservations (create, commit, release) with strong concurrency tests
Update runtime routing to mark requests as reserved or on-demand before metering hook
Add reconciliation job that replays ledger to materialized aggregates and emits discrepancy reports
Add telemetry: per-tenant drift metric, reservation-failures, reconciliation-errors
End-to-end tests + staging rollout behind feature flag, run canary for 48h, then promote
test_plan: Unit tests for aggregator (edge buckets around boundaries)
Integration test: simulate burst where reserved and on-demand run concurrently and assert no double-count
Backfill test: inject 90 days of synthetic events with known sums and verify reconciliation output
Chaos test: kill billing-service while reservation in-flight and assert reconciler fixes state
Manual verification checklist with Finance: compare sample of invoices before/after backfill
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the new ledger + aggregator behind 'quota-v2'
Deploy to staging and run a synthetic workload that mimics enterprise reserved bursts
Enable for 5 low-risk tenants in production (canary) for 48h with close monitoring
If canary green, enable for all tenants using reserved capacity, keep on-demand on legacy path for 72h
Flip on-demand to new path and monitor for 1 week, run reconciliation after 24h and compare reports
Once stable, schedule backfill for last 90 days during low-traffic window (weekend)
